decision_reason: Official GLA sources prove that LBSM2 is a non-personal property/building-level model with an Enfield extract, modelled energy-consumption variables, UPRN-linked property records and TOID building views. The canonical parcel carrier declares no UPRN, TOID or address binding, and point-to-building spatial guessing is forbidden. The Enfield resource bytes and schema header were not read in this execution and the API is available only on request. No exact canonical parcel binding or actual gas-meter value can be promoted.

source_evidence_manifest.relevant_excerpt: Wave322 completed with remote readback PASS under the same continuation key. It produced zero business rows and zero parcel bindings, and recorded that the canonical carrier has no parcel-to-UPRN or address binding.

GLA states that LBSM2 models energy consumption together with property, fabric and heating variables. The download is building-level; EPC records are matched to UPRN, and missing energy consumption is estimated from fuel-bill data. The blog distinguishes theoretical EPC-led modelling from future actual-consumption sensor inputs.

The London Building Stock Model v2 provides energy-efficiency data for all London homes, combines EPC and other sources, and uses machine learning to generate modelled values where source data is absent. The current release is based on October 2024 data; an Enfield CSV extract is listed. The dataset contains Ordnance Survey mapping and is published under OS presumption to publish, with Open Government Licence v3 shown by the London Datastore.

The LBSM2 explorer offers individual-residence views as UPRN points and building views as TOID footprints. Viewing or downloading requires acceptance of terms passed through from Ordnance Survey and the EPC data source.

source_evidence_manifest.publisher: Greater London Authority / UCL Energy Institute
source_evidence_manifest.relevant_excerpt: The original London Building Stock Model is a database of energy and carbon data for domestic and non-domestic London buildings, with an Enfield extract listed. The model snapshot is based on 2017 energy-performance information and an Ordnance Survey 2023 property list; some listed properties may have no model data attached.

source_evidence_manifest.publisher: Cabinet Office / DSIT / Government Digital Service
source_evidence_manifest.relevant_excerpt: The official algorithmic-transparency record describes a 3.8 million residential-property table with 21 variables and per-value source flags. Inputs are linked by UPRN or building location. It reports 87 percent model accuracy, states that outputs include Ordnance Survey data governed by PSGA, and warns that modelled values are not 100 percent accurate and require property surveys for detailed decisions.
